subject: Workplace Skills
title: Nudge Theory for Behavior Change
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Nudge Theory for Behavior Change.

hook.text: Changing the cafeteria layout increased healthy food choices by 25%. No rules changed. Just the arrangement.

buildup.text: Thaler and Sunstein's nudge theory says small environmental changes can significantly shift behavior.

discovery.text: A nudge preserves freedom of choice while making the desired option easier. Defaults are the most powerful nudge.

twist.text: Mandates trigger resistance. Nudges fly under the radar. People adopt the behavior without feeling controlled.

climax.text: Change the default before writing a policy. Make the right choice the easy choice and adoption soars.

punchline.text: Change the default. Behavior follows the easy path.

quiz.question: Why are nudges more effective than mandates for behavior change?
options: Nudges are legally enforceable while mandates are not
Nudges preserve choice and avoid triggering resistance
Nudges work only in food-related contexts
